items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: He and Clancy Hayes. Clancy Hayes, oh man I think he was from Parsons, Kansas and so he knew all the Mississippi River lore.

ctx.x: Well of all the people you’ve played with over the years, is there one that stands out as a terrifically interesting character?

Well Scobey was a very fine trumpet player. He loved Louis and Scobey of course had played classical music as well as jazz so his musicianship — he had excellent musicianship. He and Clancy Hayes. Clancy Hayes, oh man I think he was from Parsons, Kansas and so he knew all the Mississippi River lore. The first time I heard Scott Joplin’s name it was from Clancy Hayes. Jack Brook, excellent trombonist, excellent musician. My Dixieland experience, they were good musicians and kind of like characters. Fatha Hines,…

do your thing, play your part. And he would size you up and see what you could do, so I had an extended solo with the band. As a matter of fact I’ve got a record out, oh what the heck I’ve even forgotten what the name of it is.
